title: Power and duration trade places
hook: 100W for one hour or 20W for five: compare the energy, not just watts.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compare energy use while accounting for both constant power and duration.

misconception: Lower power always means lower total energy consumption.
objective: Compare energy use while accounting for both constant power and duration.

claims.text: Illustrative A runs at 100W for one hour; B at 20W for five hours. B’s duration stays five times A’s. Scaled model; illustrative:100W×h;20W×5h;tariff=€0.30/kWh.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At A-hours=1h, A=0.1kWh and B=0.1kWh. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",100,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",20,5,"x"],1000]; x denotes A-hours. At x=1, A=0.1, B=0.1. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Energy is power multiplied by duration. Here the fivefold duration exactly offsets the fivefold power difference. A low watt number alone cannot identify the lower energy total.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",100,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",20,5,"x"],1000]; x denotes A-hours. At x=1, A=0.1, B=0.1. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Illustrative loads: 50W for two hours, or 10W for ten hours. Which uses more energy? Correct: They use the same. Energy is power × time: both are 100Wh (0.1kWh), so the lower watt number alone did not decide it.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
